meta.title: Qwen 3.8 27B on my laptop can interpret model weights, too

comments.author: kacey
comments.text: I was sniped by Simon Willison, and did not have a chance to try this myself XD it is a response to a post from the other day about how a frontier LLM could interpret weights in models directly. Simon Willison tossed Qwen 3.8 27b at the problem and it did OK (3/4 games identified by inspecting weights directly). IMO, the takeaway should be that (1) models have probably been able to do this for like a year, except no one asked, (2) it doesn't take a frontier, billion dollar model to do this -- the one which runs on your average laptop gets most of the way there.

comments.author: kacey
comments.text:
As ruspaceni noted in the other thread, mixture of experts models -- such as Qwen 3.6 35 a3b -- work fine on relatively low amounts of VRAM by being able to efficiently spill out into system RAM. Before I blew $1300 Canadian loonies on an Arc Pro B70, I was running it on an RTX 2060 6gb card.

We've seen a few other, smaller shops train up MoE models that seem to be approaching the performance of some of Qwen's older, smaller models (e.g. Mellium2.1 12b seems to strike in the range of Qwen 3.5 9B, for instance), so it seems reasonable to assume that we'll see models that can run with less memory as time goes on. It's just that they fell out of vogue recently, presumably because the larger labs realized that they could court more favour with 100B+ models that compete directly with the present day frontier, rather than replicating performance from 6-12 months ago.

comments.author: kacey
comments.text:
I'm largely quoting the article, and added "average" in order to underline that a multi-million dollar datacentre was not used in this effort. The assertion of this post is that the startling result from the other day was, in fact, relatively mundane. The LLMs aren't suddenly evolving into Skynet or anything; their capabilities are just slowly improving/are stationary (given that Astra is surely like a hundred+ orders of magnitude larger than Qwen 3.8 27b and provided less than a hundred orders of magnitude better results).


I’m delighted to share that Qwen 3.8 27B running on my laptop can do this as well!


Understood that "average" might have tweaked some people; apologies for using such language.
